subject: BridgePoint private cluster: sustained queue plateau and p95 rise - request for exec sync
messages:
From: Alejandra Cruz <alejandra.cruz@bridgepoint.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Elliot Song <elliot.song@bridgepoint.ai>, Karim Farouk <kfarouk@bridgepoint.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Persistent queue plateau + p95 latency rise on private cluster (urgent)

Hi Tessa —

We started seeing a steady plateau in request queue depth on our private deployment late yesterday, accompanied by a rise in p95 latency from ~420ms to ~1.6s and a 503 rate creeping up to 1.8% at peak. This is across our mid-tier model route (gpt-open-8b-q).

Quick summary of what we've observed:
- Increased queue depth on nodes 3/4/5 in our VPC private cluster (attached time-series and ndjson logs).
- TCP retransmits and occasional kernel-level socket timeouts correlated with the latency spikes.
- No recent config changes on our side; the last platform change we see is an automatic model-variant roll (redwood-side) at 02:14 UTC.

Impact: customer-facing inference is degraded for our ER use-case; we're seeing ~8% drop in successful throughput and customer SLA alerts firing.

Immediate asks: can Redwood triage the roll and provide a short remediation plan? If this looks like a runtime kernel or batching regression, we need an exec sync today — our CTO is requesting an update and potential credits if the SLA breach continues.

I attached: diagnostics-20280608.tar.gz (system traces + pprof), service-logs-bridgepoint-20280608.ndjson

Thanks,
Alejandra Cruz
Head of Cloud Ops | BridgePoint AI
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Alejandra Cruz <alejandra.cruz@bridgepoint.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Persistent queue plateau + p95 latency rise on private cluster (urgent)

Alejandra — thank you for the quick summary and the artifacts. We're on it.

Immediate actions from Redwood today:
1) I have escalated to Engineering (Vivek) to prioritize triage and to check the recent model-variant rollout.
2) We're standing up a 30-minute war room at 11:00 PT to align on mitigation steps (invite sent).
3) Temporary mitigations we'll try in the first hour: pin to prior model-variant on a subset of nodes, reduce max-batch-size to lower tail latency, and enable aggressive prefix caching for identical traffic.

Please confirm who from your infra team will join the 11:00 PT call and whether we can test the model-variant rollback on a single availability zone first.

Link to runbook + artifacts: https://drive.redwood.com/BRIDGE-3742/diagnostics

I'll follow up after the war room with a remediation timeline and any exec-level notes you can share with your CTO.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

---
Attachment: diagnostics-20280608.tar.gz (application/gzip)
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Alejandra Cruz <alejandra.cruz@bridgepoint.ai>, Elliot Song <elliot.song@bridgepoint.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Persistent queue plateau + p95 latency rise on private cluster (urgent)

Thanks team — triage notes from the war room:

Observations:
- The automatic model-variant roll at 02:14 UTC introduced a q8 quantized variant with a new fused-kernel set. Perf tests in canary showed parity but production traffic exhibits higher KV cache churn and larger per-request decode time for sequences >512 tokens.
- Nodes 3/4/5 show elevated syscall latency and softirqs consistent with network stack backpressure; packet drop counters higher on node NICs.
- Batching effectively increased per-token latency under current traffic shape; combined with KV cache misses this pushed p95 beyond our SLOs.

Short-term mitigations we executed (11:15–11:45 PT):
- Rolled model-variant back to prior non-fused kernel on 25% of the fleet (AZ-1). Observed p95 drop from ~1.6s to ~520ms on those nodes within 12 minutes.
- Reduced max_batch_tokens from 2048->1024 on hot routes to reduce tail amplification.
- Enabled aggressive KV cache pinning for frequent prefixes (reduces cold-start churn).

Next steps (recommended within 24h):
- Full rollback of the fused-kernel variant until kernel selection tests are expanded (we recommend a 48h canary with synthetic traffic to exercise long sequences).
- Investigate NIC configurations on customer nodes (we saw mismatched MTU settings on node-4) — request BridgePoint infra to confirm NIC offload and MTU.
- Nightly job to pre-warm KV cache for top-500 prefixes and warm shards prior to business hours.
- Engineering will prepare a short exec memo describing cause, actions taken, and a proposed timeline for re-introducing the fused-kernel variant.

If BridgePoint wants an exec readout we can prepare a 1-page for your CTO by EOD. Also flagging potential SLA credit exposure; I'll coordinate with Marissa and Laura on the financial/CS side.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
From: Karim Farouk <kfarouk@bridgepoint.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Alejandra Cruz <alejandra.cruz@bridgepoint.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jun 2028 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Persistent queue plateau + p95 latency rise on private cluster (urgent)

Thanks — appreciate the rapid response. We approved the rollback in the war room and confirmed the MTU mismatch on node-4 (our infra team applied the corrected settings at 13:20 PT).

Request: yes, please send the 1-page exec memo for our CTO (cc'd Alejandra) — he needs:
- concise root cause (2–3 bullets)
- actions taken and immediate mitigations (what changed and when)
- next steps and timeline to reintroduce the fused-kernel variant safely
- any proposed customer credits/remediation and the associated calculation (throughput loss window and affected tokens)

We also want an Ops-to-Ops postmortem scheduled next week to walk through NIC tuning and pre-warm jobs — can Redwood own the runbook changes?

Karim Farouk
CTO, BridgePoint AI
